subject: nuclear explosion
title: The 5 Biggest Nuclear Explosions Ever, Ranked (#1 Was Set to Half Power)

scenes.text: The five biggest nuclear explosions ever, ranked. Hiroshima would not even register on this chart.

scenes.label: Castle Bravo · 15 megatons
scenes.text: Number five: Castle Bravo, 1954. Fifteen megatons, two and a half times what its designers expected. The fallout covered 7,000 square miles of the Pacific.

scenes.label: Soviet Test 173 · 19 megatons
scenes.text: Number four: Soviet Test 173, September 1962. Nineteen megatons, fired over the Arctic weeks before the Cuban Missile Crisis.

scenes.label: Soviet Test 147 · 21 megatons
scenes.text: Number three: Test 147, August 1962. Twenty-one megatons, about 1,400 Hiroshimas. It doesn't even have a name.

scenes.label: Soviet Test 219 · 24 megatons
scenes.text: Number two: Test 219, Christmas Eve 1962. Twenty-four megatons, one of the last bombs dropped from a plane before the test ban.

scenes.label: Tsar Bomba · 50 megatons
scenes.text: Number one: Tsar Bomba, 1961. Fifty megatons. The cloud rose 60 kilometers, the flash was seen 1,000 kilometers away. And it was built for one hundred.

description:
The five most powerful nuclear explosions in history, ranked by yield.
Castle Bravo (USA, 1954) reached 15 megatons, two and a half times its expected yield, and spread fallout over about 7,000 square miles. The Soviet Union's Test 173 (19.1 Mt), Test 147 (21.1 Mt) and Test 219 (24.2 Mt) were all detonated over Novaya Zemlya in 1962. Tsar Bomba, 30 October 1961, yielded 50 megatons: its mushroom cloud climbed more than 60 km, its flash was visible about 1,000 km away, and it had been designed for 100 megatons. The Hiroshima bomb was about 0.015 megatons.
Which of these had you never heard of?
first_comment: Tsar Bomba reportedly damaged buildings more than 160 kilometres from ground zero. Which would you have put at number one? And what should we rank next: the biggest explosions that were not nuclear?
